metadata.title: Disk rigidity for attained complete polynomial Crouzeix equality
metadata.description:
Relative to the pinned complete Crouzeix inequality and its exterior Faber operations, and to Jin's geometric circle criterion, we prove that actual factor-two equality for one finite matrix-valued polynomial forces the numerical range to be a nondegenerate disk in every finite dimension. We retain the Jensen deficit in finite diagonal dual tests. Strong exterior boundary convergence and a triple-variance Fatou argument then make the diagonal compressed resolvents constant, without a rank-one assumption. An ordered constant test and equality in Parseval produce a fixed matrix polynomial channel that is unitary on the boundary. Its rational inverse is holomorphic in the exterior and vanishes at infinity. The determinant therefore realizes the boundary as a full polynomial level set. The numerical-range Hermitian tangent pencil supplies the additional hypothesis of the credited circle criterion. The argument allows coefficient rank greater than one and assumes no initial boundary smoothness.

This is an AI-assisted preprint with internal independent agent proof, contribution and manuscript reviews, not external peer review. Supporting Lean material is partial and does not formalize the complete theorem. Mathematical results from OpenAI/math at revision fd4aeeb2ee4fc729c18d98444fed42fd0529eeeb are stipulated premises, with exact source interfaces and other credited inputs disclosed in the paper. The literature comparison is bounded and does not certify worldwide priority.

Formal coverage: Three finite real scalar variance declarations compile and have independent type/axiom audit. The Hilbert-valued integral, Fatou, exterior convergence, rationalization and geometric arguments are not formalized.
